precepts.why:
“The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.”

Christ ends the enmity of the split. From Rehoboam and Jeroboam, through the golden calves, through Pekah and Rezin and the Assyrian captivity, Judah and Ephraim were enemies, and the Jews had no dealings with the Samaritans. Now Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim. That is why Peter came to Cornelius “without gainsaying, as soon as I was sent for.”

precepts.text: The Most High looked upon the children of Israel and had respect unto them, so he does respect Israel by nation.
precepts.point: Peter opens his mouth and says the Most High is no respecter of persons, but in every nation he that feareth him and worketh righteousness is accepted, and the word was sent unto the children of Israel. "No respecter of persons" does not mean nations are equal, because the Most High plainly had respect unto Israel and chose Israel above all people; it means he does not respect persons in judgment concerning his law, so whether a man sins outside the law or inside it he is judged.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Peter says, “Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons.” That does not mean the nations are equal. “And God looked upon the children of Israel, and God had respect unto them.”

The Most High plainly had respect unto Israel and chose Israel above all people. He does respect Israel by nation. So “no respecter of persons” has to mean something else.

precepts.text: It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment, which is the kind of respect being denied.
precepts.point: Peter opens his mouth and says the Most High is no respecter of persons, but in every nation he that feareth him and worketh righteousness is accepted, and the word was sent unto the children of Israel. "No respecter of persons" does not mean nations are equal, because the Most High plainly had respect unto Israel and chose Israel above all people; it means he does not respect persons in judgment concerning his law, so whether a man sins outside the law or inside it he is judged.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment.”

That is the kind of respect being denied. The Most High does not respect persons in judgment concerning his law. Whether a man sins outside the law or inside it, he is judged. He chose Israel by nation, but he does not excuse a man in judgment because of who he is.

precepts.text: Tribulation and wrath upon every soul that doeth evil, of the Jew first and also of the Gentile, for there is no respect of persons with the Most High.
precepts.point: Peter opens his mouth and says the Most High is no respecter of persons, but in every nation he that feareth him and worketh righteousness is accepted, and the word was sent unto the children of Israel. "No respecter of persons" does not mean nations are equal, because the Most High plainly had respect unto Israel and chose Israel above all people; it means he does not respect persons in judgment concerning his law, so whether a man sins outside the law or inside it he is judged.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile; But glory, honour, and peace, to every man that worketh good, to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile: For there is no respect of persons with God.”

No respect of persons means judgment by the law: evil is repaid and good is rewarded, whoever does it. And it says the Jew first, and also the Gentile, because prophecy set Judah, Benjamin and Levi to rise up first. The Gentiles are the dispersed northern tribes scattered among the heathen.

precepts.text: The Most High saves the tents of Judah first, so Judah wakes up before the rest.
precepts.point: It says "the Jew first, and also the Gentile" because prophecy set Judah, Benjamin, and Levi to rise up first, and the "Gentiles" are the dispersed northern tribes scattered among the heathen, left few in number. This is the diaspora, the same scattering some now call the African diaspora.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.”

That is why it is “the Jew first.” The Most High saves the tents of Judah first, so Judah wakes up before the rest. Then come the Gentiles, the northern tribes.

precepts.text: The Jews ask whether Christ will go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles and teach the Gentiles, meaning the scattered of Israel.
precepts.point: It says "the Jew first, and also the Gentile" because prophecy set Judah, Benjamin, and Levi to rise up first, and the "Gentiles" are the dispersed northern tribes scattered among the heathen, left few in number. This is the diaspora, the same scattering some now call the African diaspora.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?”

The dispersed among the Gentiles are the scattered of Israel. When the Jews asked whether Christ would go and teach the Gentiles, they meant Israelites dispersed among the nations. That is who the Gentiles are in Peter's word: the northern tribes in the diaspora.

precepts.text: Israel defiled their own land, so the Most High scattered them among the heathen and dispersed them through the countries.
precepts.point: It says "the Jew first, and also the Gentile" because prophecy set Judah, Benjamin, and Levi to rise up first, and the "Gentiles" are the dispersed northern tribes scattered among the heathen, left few in number. This is the diaspora, the same scattering some now call the African diaspora.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Son of man, when the house of Israel dwelt in their own land, they defiled it by their own way and by their doings.” “Wherefore I poured my fury upon them for the blood that they had shed upon the land, and for their idols wherewith they had polluted it: And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries.”

That is how Israel came to be “in every nation.” Israel defiled their own land, so the Most High scattered them among the heathen and dispersed them through the countries. This is the diaspora, the same scattering some now call the African diaspora.

precepts.text: James writes to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad among the heathen.
precepts.point: It says "the Jew first, and also the Gentile" because prophecy set Judah, Benjamin, and Levi to rise up first, and the "Gentiles" are the dispersed northern tribes scattered among the heathen, left few in number. This is the diaspora, the same scattering some now call the African diaspora.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.”

James writes to the twelve tribes scattered abroad among the heathen. That is the “every nation” of Peter's word: not every race, but every nation where Israel was scattered.

precepts.text: The Most High will scatter Israel among the nations and leave them few in number among the heathen.
precepts.point: It says "the Jew first, and also the Gentile" because prophecy set Judah, Benjamin, and Levi to rise up first, and the "Gentiles" are the dispersed northern tribes scattered among the heathen, left few in number. This is the diaspora, the same scattering some now call the African diaspora.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.”

The Gentiles are the dispersed northern tribes, scattered among the heathen and left few in number. That is who Peter means when he says “in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.”

precepts.text: It became unlawful to keep the Sabbath or be a Jew, and Israel was forced to conform to the Gentiles or die.
precepts.point: Once scattered, they were mingled among the nations, learned their works, served their idols, and by decree were forbidden to keep the Sabbath or the feasts or even to call themselves a Jew, forced to conform to the manners of the Gentiles on pain of death. This is the same butchering endured in slavery, where it became unlawful to hold any Israelite name, custom, or nationality.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Once scattered, they were mingled among the nations, learned their works and served their idols. And by decree they were forbidden to keep their law: “Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.”

They were “brought by bitter constraint to eat of the sacrifices”, and a decree went out “that they should observe the same fashions, and be partakers of their sacrifices: And whoso would not conform themselves to the manners of the Gentiles should be put to death. Then might a man have seen the present misery.”

This is the same butchering endured in slavery, where it became unlawful to hold any Israelite name, custom or nationality. That is how Israelites became Gentiles in the flesh, in every nation.

precepts.text: Christ dwells in the borders of Zebulun and Naphtali, "Galilee of the Gentiles," and the people in darkness see a great light.
precepts.point: "Galilee of the Gentiles" proves the point, because those northern tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali, broken and driven into darkness, are the people who saw the great light when Christ came preaching, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand." They sat in the shadow of death because Ephraim was broken and taken into Assyria.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Christ “came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles; The people which sat in darkness saw great light.”

“Galilee of the Gentiles” proves the point. Zebulun and Naphtali are northern tribes, broken and driven into darkness, and they are the people who saw the great light when Christ came preaching repentance, for the kingdom of heaven was at hand. They sat in the shadow of death because Ephraim was broken and taken into Assyria.

precepts.text: The spoil of Samaria is taken before the king of Assyria, whose flood overflows the land, and the people shall be broken in pieces.
precepts.point: "Galilee of the Gentiles" proves the point, because those northern tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali, broken and driven into darkness, are the people who saw the great light when Christ came preaching, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand." They sat in the shadow of death because Ephraim was broken and taken into Assyria.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“The riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of Assyria.” Because the people refused “the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah’s son”, the Lord brought up upon them “the waters of the river, strong and many, even the king of Assyria, and all his glory.”

“He shall come up over all his channels, and go over all his banks”, and “gird yourselves, and ye shall be broken in pieces.” That is Ephraim broken and carried into Assyria, the beginning of the darkness the northern tribes sat in.

precepts.text: They are hungry, curse their king and their God, and are driven to darkness, dimness, and anguish.
precepts.point: "Galilee of the Gentiles" proves the point, because those northern tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali, broken and driven into darkness, are the people who saw the great light when Christ came preaching, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand." They sat in the shadow of death because Ephraim was broken and taken into Assyria.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“And they shall pass through it, hardly bestead and hungry: and it shall come to pass, that when they shall be hungry, they shall fret themselves, and curse their king and their God.”

“And they shall look unto the earth; and behold trouble and darkness, dimness of anguish; and they shall be driven to darkness.” That is the northern kingdom after the Assyrian flood: driven into darkness. These are the people who sat in darkness until Christ came.

precepts.text: The land of Zebulun and Naphtali, the people that walked in darkness, have seen a great light.
precepts.point: "Galilee of the Gentiles" proves the point, because those northern tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali, broken and driven into darkness, are the people who saw the great light when Christ came preaching, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand." They sat in the shadow of death because Ephraim was broken and taken into Assyria.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Nevertheless the dimness shall not be such as was in her vexation, when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.”

“The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.” The land of Zebulun and Naphtali, the northern tribes driven into darkness, are the ones who saw the great light. That light is Christ, and Matthew says so plainly.

precepts.text: Manasseh and Ephraim are named together, confirming the darkened people are the northern tribes.
precepts.point: "Galilee of the Gentiles" proves the point, because those northern tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali, broken and driven into darkness, are the people who saw the great light when Christ came preaching, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand." They sat in the shadow of death because Ephraim was broken and taken into Assyria.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Manasseh, Ephraim; and Ephraim, Manasseh: and they together shall be against Judah.”

Manasseh and Ephraim are named together, and that confirms who the darkened people are: the northern tribes. The people of Galilee of the Gentiles who walked in darkness are Israel's north, set against Judah, and they are the Gentiles Peter speaks of.

precepts.text: Such as sit in darkness and the shadow of death, bound in affliction and iron, are the scattered Israelites.
precepts.point: "Galilee of the Gentiles" proves the point, because those northern tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali, broken and driven into darkness, are the people who saw the great light when Christ came preaching, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand." They sat in the shadow of death because Ephraim was broken and taken into Assyria.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Such as sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, being bound in affliction and iron.”

Those that sit in darkness and the shadow of death, bound in affliction and iron, are the scattered Israelites. That is the same people of whom Matthew says, “to them which sat in the region and shadow of death light is sprung up.”

precepts.text: There were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven, because Israel was scattered everywhere.
precepts.point: So "in every nation" means the diaspora of Israel, devout men out of every nation under heaven, and the peace Peter preaches is Christ, Shiloh, unto whom the gathering of the people shall be. He is Lord of all the twelve tribes.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.”

So “in every nation” means the diaspora of Israel: devout men out of every nation under heaven, because Israel was scattered everywhere. When Peter says “in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him”, he is speaking of those Israelites.

precepts.text: The sceptre stays with Judah until Shiloh come, and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.
precepts.point: So "in every nation" means the diaspora of Israel, devout men out of every nation under heaven, and the peace Peter preaches is Christ, Shiloh, unto whom the gathering of the people shall be. He is Lord of all the twelve tribes.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.”

The peace Peter preaches is Christ, Shiloh, unto whom the gathering of the people shall be. “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ: (he is Lord of all:)”. He is Lord of all the twelve tribes, gathering Judah first and then the scattered of every nation.

precepts.text: Paul's heart's desire and prayer for Israel is that they might be saved, defining the "whosoever."
precepts.point: The "whosoever" is whosoever of Israel, of Zion, because Paul opens the same subject praying for Israel to be saved, and the stone laid in Zion is Christ, so those who believe on him shall not be ashamed.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Peter ends his rehearsal of Christ's ministry with this: “To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.” The whosoever is whosoever of Israel, of Zion.

Paul opens the same subject praying for Israel: “Brethren, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.” That defines the whosoever. The salvation he is speaking of is Israel's.

precepts.text: The scripture saith, whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.
precepts.point: The "whosoever" is whosoever of Israel, of Zion, because Paul opens the same subject praying for Israel to be saved, and the stone laid in Zion is Christ, so those who believe on him shall not be ashamed.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.”

Paul says this in the same chapter where his prayer is for Israel to be saved. The scripture he is quoting is the stone laid in Zion, and the whosoever that believes on that stone is whosoever of Zion, whosoever of Israel.

precepts.text: The Most High lays in Zion a tried, precious cornerstone, and he that believeth shall not be ashamed.
precepts.point: The "whosoever" is whosoever of Israel, of Zion, because Paul opens the same subject praying for Israel to be saved, and the stone laid in Zion is Christ, so those who believe on him shall not be ashamed.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste.”

The stone laid in Zion is Christ. Those who believe on him shall not be ashamed. The stone is laid in Zion, and the believer Isaiah speaks of is in Zion. That is the whosoever of Peter's word.

precepts.text: Zion is the city of David, which is Israel, so believing "in Zion" is believing in Israel.
precepts.point: The "whosoever" is whosoever of Israel, of Zion, because Paul opens the same subject praying for Israel to be saved, and the stone laid in Zion is Christ, so those who believe on him shall not be ashamed.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes “that they might bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which is Zion.”

Zion is the city of David, which is Israel. So the stone laid in Zion is laid in Israel, and believing in Zion is believing in Israel. The whosoever that receives remission of sins through his name is whosoever of Israel.

precepts.text: The covenant with the house of Israel: he writes the law in their hearts, forgives their iniquity, and remembers their sin no more.
precepts.point: Remission of sins, the forgiveness and canceling of the debt, is the new covenant made with the house of Israel, not with every nation. The Most High promised to forgive Israel's iniquity and remember their sins no more.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Remission of sins is the forgiveness and canceling of the debt, and it is the new covenant made with the house of Israel, not with every nation. “But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the Lord, I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people.”

“For I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.” The Most High promised to forgive Israel's iniquity and remember their sins no more. That is the remission of sins Peter preached in Cornelius' house.

precepts.text: The same covenant with the house of Israel, forgiving their unrighteousness and remembering their sins no more.
precepts.point: Remission of sins, the forgiveness and canceling of the debt, is the new covenant made with the house of Israel, not with every nation. The Most High promised to forgive Israel's iniquity and remember their sins no more.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
The same covenant is written again in Hebrews: “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts.”

“For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.” It is the house of Israel whose sins are remembered no more. Remission of sins belongs to that covenant.

precepts.text: Blessed be the Most High of Israel, who redeemed his people and gives knowledge of salvation unto them by the remission of their sins.
precepts.point: Remission of sins, the forgiveness and canceling of the debt, is the new covenant made with the house of Israel, not with every nation. The Most High promised to forgive Israel's iniquity and remember their sins no more.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David.”

It is “the mercy promised to our fathers”, his holy covenant, “The oath which he sware to our father Abraham.” And John was sent before the face of the Lord “To give knowledge of salvation unto his people by the remission of their sins.”

Remission of sins was given unto his people, Israel, the people the Lord God of Israel visited and redeemed. That is the remission all the prophets gave witness to.

precepts.text: Peter tells the same people to repent and be baptized for the remission of sins, the forgiveness of sins.
precepts.point: Remission of sins, the forgiveness and canceling of the debt, is the new covenant made with the house of Israel, not with every nation. The Most High promised to forgive Israel's iniquity and remember their sins no more.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.”

Peter told the same people, the men of Israel, to repent and be baptized for the remission of sins, the forgiveness of sins. It is the same message he brought to Cornelius: “through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.”

precepts.text: Sin is the transgression of the law, so only those given the law can break it and need remission.
precepts.point: Only Israel could receive remission because sin is the transgression of the law, and the law and the first testament of animal sacrifice were given to Israel alone. Christ's blood was shed for the many of the nation of Israel who were under that first covenant.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.”

Only Israel could receive remission, because sin is the transgression of the law, and the law was given to Israel alone. Only those given the law can break it and need remission of it.

precepts.text: The name of the Most High is found nowhere but in Israel, not among the nations.
precepts.point: Only Israel could receive remission because sin is the transgression of the law, and the law and the first testament of animal sacrifice were given to Israel alone. Christ's blood was shed for the many of the nation of Israel who were under that first covenant.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Weigh thou therefore our wickedness now in the balance, and their’s also that dwell the world; and so shall thy name no where be found but in Israel.”

The name of the Most High is found nowhere but in Israel, not among the nations. So remission of sins “through his name” is found in Israel.

precepts.text: His blood of the new testament is shed for many for the remission of sins, the many of Israel.
precepts.point: Only Israel could receive remission because sin is the transgression of the law, and the law and the first testament of animal sacrifice were given to Israel alone. Christ's blood was shed for the many of the nation of Israel who were under that first covenant.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.”

Christ's blood was shed for the many of the nation of Israel who were under the first covenant. The new testament is the covenant with the house of Israel, and the many are the many of Israel.

precepts.text: He is mediator of the new testament by means of death for the redemption of transgressions under the first testament.
precepts.point: Only Israel could receive remission because sin is the transgression of the law, and the law and the first testament of animal sacrifice were given to Israel alone. Christ's blood was shed for the many of the nation of Israel who were under that first covenant.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.”

Christ died for the transgressions that were under the first testament. The first testament of animal sacrifice was given to Israel alone, so the redemption is for those who were under it.

precepts.text: Moses sprinkles the blood of the covenant on the people of Israel by the twelve pillars, so only Israel was under the first covenant.
precepts.point: Only Israel could receive remission because sin is the transgression of the law, and the law and the first testament of animal sacrifice were given to Israel alone. Christ's blood was shed for the many of the nation of Israel who were under that first covenant.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“And Moses wrote all the words of the Lord, and rose up early in the morning, and builded an altar under the hill, and twelve pillars, according to the twelve tribes of Israel.”

He took the book of the covenant and read it to the people, “and they said, All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient. And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which the Lord hath made with you concerning all these words.”

The blood of the first covenant was sprinkled on the people of Israel, by twelve pillars for the twelve tribes. Only Israel was under the first covenant, and so only Israel is redeemed from its transgressions.

precepts.text: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ.
precepts.point: The purpose is that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern tribes, through Christ, who redeemed the twelve tribes from the curse of the law given to Israel. "All nations blessed in Abraham" means the tribes within Abraham's seed, not every nation on earth.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree.” That is the one “whom they slew and hanged on a tree.”

“That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.” The Gentiles here are the northern tribes. Christ redeemed the twelve tribes from the curse of the law given to Israel, so that the blessing of Abraham might come on them.

precepts.text: Cursed is he that confirmeth not all the words of this law, a curse commanded to the people of Israel.
precepts.point: The purpose is that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern tribes, through Christ, who redeemed the twelve tribes from the curse of the law given to Israel. "All nations blessed in Abraham" means the tribes within Abraham's seed, not every nation on earth.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. And all the people shall say, Amen.”

This is the curse of the law, and it was commanded to the people of Israel. They are the ones who said Amen to it. So the ones Christ redeemed from the curse of the law are Israel.

precepts.text: All the nations of the earth blessed in Abraham means the tribes of his seed, for Abraham did not father every nation.
precepts.point: The purpose is that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern tribes, through Christ, who redeemed the twelve tribes from the curse of the law given to Israel. "All nations blessed in Abraham" means the tribes within Abraham's seed, not every nation on earth.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?”

All nations blessed in Abraham means the tribes within Abraham's seed, not every nation on earth, for Abraham did not father every nation. The blessing of Abraham that comes on the Gentiles through Christ comes on the tribes of his seed.

precepts.text: In Abraham's seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed, and that seed is Christ blessing the twelve tribes.
precepts.point: The purpose is that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern tribes, through Christ, who redeemed the twelve tribes from the curse of the law given to Israel. "All nations blessed in Abraham" means the tribes within Abraham's seed, not every nation on earth.

Cornelius says they are all present before the Most High to hear all things commanded of God.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: Peter opens his mouth and says the Most High is no respecter of persons, but in every nation he that feareth him and worketh righteousness is accepted, and the word was sent unto the children of Israel. "No respecter of persons" does not mean nations are equal, because the Most High plainly had respect unto Israel and chose Israel above all people; it means he does not respect persons in judgment concerning his law, so whether a man sins outside the law or inside it he is judged.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: "Galilee of the Gentiles" proves the point, because those northern tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali, broken and driven into darkness, are the people who saw the great light when Christ came preaching, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand." They sat in the shadow of death because Ephraim was broken and taken into Assyria.

So "in every nation" means the diaspora of Israel, devout men out of every nation under heaven, and the peace Peter preaches is Christ, Shiloh, unto whom the gathering of the people shall be. He is Lord of all the twelve tribes.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: Peter rehearses the ministry of Christ, published throughout Judea from Galilee, how the Most High anointed Jesus of Nazareth, who went about doing good and healing all oppressed of the devil, whom they slew and hanged on a tree, and whom the Most High raised the third day and shewed openly to chosen witnesses. To him all the prophets witness that through his name whosoever believeth receiveth remission of sins.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: Remission of sins, the forgiveness and canceling of the debt, is the new covenant made with the house of Israel, not with every nation. The Most High promised to forgive Israel's iniquity and remember their sins no more.

Only Israel could receive remission because sin is the transgression of the law, and the law and the first testament of animal sacrifice were given to Israel alone. Christ's blood was shed for the many of the nation of Israel who were under that first covenant.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: While Peter yet spake, the Holy Ghost fell on all who heard, and they of the circumcision were astonished that on the "Gentiles" also the gift was poured out, for they spake with tongues and magnified the Most High. The Spirit is poured only on the house of Israel, so the Gentiles receiving it are the children of Israel, the northern kingdom.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In
